argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower certification rationale than a clean-certification reading. Aggregate readiness clears launch by 2.2 percentage points and rehearsal shows no severity-one incidents, which supports release-level certification. The same record also shows a remaining weakness in the tax filing assistant use case, concentrated in deduction eligibility explanation, and a draft-only mitigation artifact with TBD owner and threshold. On that evidence, the supportable position is certification with explicit model-card disclosure of the tax-use-case limitation, not certification on the theory that the draft runbook eliminates the disclosure obligation.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to resolve the audit issue. The remaining uncertainty is governance-framing uncertainty, not evidence that the release as a whole failed readiness. That uncertainty can be handled by treating the certification as caveated and requiring the limitation to be disclosed, rather than escalating as though the record supported only outright noncompliance.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not support unconditional certification here. The policy text says certification without material caveats requires either current evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show either condition is satisfied. It does, however, support caveated certification if the packet is framed around disclosure of the known limitation rather than denial of its materiality or reliance on the incomplete draft mitigation.
concessions: The current record does not support clean certification without material caveats.
The draft runbook does not satisfy the policy standard for an approved mitigation because required fields remain incomplete.
The model-card draft language stating there are no known material limitations is not supportable on the present record.
The record provided here does not itself prove that the final model card has already been updated to include the required limitation disclosure.
